name: code.market

sources.title: Homepage — 'Curatorial Network & Digital Product Catalog' (Codemarket OÜ); top nav has 'Submit to Newsletter'
Daily Digest page — 'A daily dose of products published on code.market... Want yours here? Just submit it.' Submit links to /newsletter/submit
Newsletter submit page — JS-rendered shell ('Loading...'); form fields not visible to static fetch
Batch-provided submission URL — renders the standard site shell; submit UI is JS-gated behind login

requirements: Catalog skews toward code products: themes, templates, app source code, plugins (WordPress/React/Flutter/Unity categories); a generic SaaS may fit only via the AI Tools category or newsletter
A Login link exists — the product-submit UI is JS-gated and likely requires a code.market account (GitHub login was historically used)

The changelog states code.market 'no longer sells third-party products, no longer processes payments on behalf of authors' — the old marketplace listing flow is deprecated; current free exposure is the newsletter/catalog
preparation: Product name, URL, description, and a fitting category (framework niches or AI tools)
A code.market account (GitHub auth historically supported)
Decide target: product in the catalog vs. a slot in the daily email digest
workflow: Open https://code.market/newsletter/submit in an interactive browser (form is client-rendered)
Alternatively sign in and use the product-submit settings (/?settings=submit-product) to add a catalog entry
Digest submissions appear in the daily email 'in random order'
watchFor: Site is JS-heavy — all submit surfaces render 'Loading...' to static fetches
Deprecated marketplace history: old 'sell your code for 70% commission' docs are stale; do not rely on author/sale features
Catalog taxonomy is dominated by IPTV/game/script categories — a SaaS launch may look out of place; the newsletter is the more general route
'Free Backlink Exchange' nav link is a separate reciprocal-link program, not a listing
countsAsLive: The product appears in a code.market catalog category page or is included in the Daily Digest email/archive
unknowns: Whether newsletter/catalog submission is free or paid — no pricing surfaced on fetched pages
Exact form fields and auth requirements on /newsletter/submit
